newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Train derailed as Romanian heat wave bends tracks.
newsitem.headline: Train derailed as Romanian heat wave bends tracks.

text.p: A dozen people were hurt when a Romanian passenger train leapt off tracks which had buckled in the sun in the most dramatic incident of a week-long heatwave, authorities said on Monday.
Four carriages came off the rails in the south of the country on Sunday in temperatures of up to 54 Celsius (129 Fahrenheit). Authorities said all the injuries had been minor.

In Bucharest, a pensioner died from a stroke on Sunday while walking outside, despite local authority warnings, as the temperature reached 37 C (98 F) in the shade. A number of people were taken to hospitals with severe sunstroke.
The heat wave has also caused hailstorms which have injured several people and brought down power and telephone lines.
But officials said negligence was the real cause of the train crash.
"Our enemy was not only the heat, but also carelessnes of those who should have taken standard safety measures in the case of hot weather," Transport Minister Traian Basescu said.
Forecasts for this week predict slightly cooler weather, with maximum temperatures of up to 26 C (79 F).
Hot summers are not unusual in Romania, where average temperatures usually exceed 30 C (86 F) throughout July and August.
